A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMD-based human-object interaction framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results for single-task and long-horizon interactions, including baseline comparisons and component ablations in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains those simulation results and adds planner evaluations, threshold sensitivity results, and a user study in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The proposed RMD representation, planner, goal construction, rewards, policy architecture, and default 0.9 transition threshold remain unchanged. Alternative VLMs and simplified prompts are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a planner generalization test using 100 HOI tasks involving 50 objects absent from InterPlay. This extends evaluation to unseen assets; the original dataset, six interaction tasks, and static/dynamic/hybrid coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds comparisons against LLaVA-1.6 and Qwen-VL-Max planner variants alongside GPT-4V and its simplified-prompt variant. Comparator membership in the original benchmark Tables 2–3 is unchanged, including UniHSI despite its omission from v3's single-task reimplementation list.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain stable. Appendices E–F introduce manual planner-label and part-decomposition assessments, VLM/prompt comparisons, a 0.80–0.95 threshold sweep, and a study where 20 participants each rate 20 sequences for realism and task consistency on 0–5 scales.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained representation, encoding, and VLM-versus-LLM ablations, v3 adds analyses of planner-model choice, prompt simplification, contradictory RMD labels, decomposition of unseen objects, and transition-threshold sensitivity. These substantially expand scrutiny of planner reliability and robustness.

E5.justification: Table 7 introduces ± quantities for user-study ratings, whereas v2 reports point estimates. Their statistical meaning and aggregation are unspecified; training-seed and repeated-run uncertainty reporting are not added.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–3 remain identical. v3 adds Tables 5–7, contradictory-label rates of 8.9%, 11.2%, and 14.7%, and 7 unreasonable part decompositions among 100 novel-object cases. New user ratings include 4.0±0.4 for realism and 4.1±0.3 for task consistency for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–16, including the piecewise RMD reward in Appendix C, are unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: unified physics-based HOI, VLM-guided RMD for automatic goals and rewards, and InterPlay. The additional experiments support existing claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Existing single-agent and long-horizon planning limitations move from Appendix E to Section 6. New discussion addresses privileged simulation states, deployment under partial observation, distillation and plan verification, while Appendix E interprets planner-error tolerance and unseen-object decomposition.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit 60 Hz simulator and 30 Hz policy-update frequencies reported in v2's implementation details. Architecture, hyperparameter tables, detailed prompts, and the project link remain available. This is reduced documentation, not evidence that the frequencies changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ji et al. (2025), Towards Immersive Human-X Interaction, and Zhang et al. (2025), OpenHOI. The existing research positioning remains substantially intact; most reference changes reflect author-year formatting.

P1.justification: v3 polishes evaluation and ablation prose, removes repetition, updates affiliation information, and reorganizes the ending sections. Limitations move into the main text, new appendices and statements appear, and the earlier broader-social-impact paragraph is removed. Most existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR headers and typography, adjusts captions and table formatting, and adds Tables 5–7. The hyperparameter table moves and becomes Table 4. Existing illustrations and qualitative sequences are retained, with appendix figures renumbered rather than redrawn.

improvement.justification: Appendices E–F provide useful new evidence about planner reliability, sensitivity, and perceived motion quality, while Section 6 clarifies deployment assumptions. These gains are tempered by undefined ± statistics, omitted simulation frequencies, and Appendix G's claim of no human subjects contradicting the 20-participant study. Overall, the additions provide a limited net improvement while leaving the core method and benchmark results unchanged.
